conventions.convention: Canonical coordinates are grouped as (q,p); J has blocks (0,I;-I,0), ω=Σdqᶦ∧dpᵢ, X_H=J∇H and contraction of X_H with ω equals dH. Complex transposes are ordinary transposes, without conjugation.

Velocity Verlet is kick-half, drift-full, kick-half. Algebraic admissibility requires every intermediate point in U; identification with local flows additionally requires whole intermediate segments in U.

The analytic splitting is A-half, B-full, A-half; potential-first analytic labels produce velocity Verlet. U is bounded and star-shaped about zero, the extensions are holomorphic on D(ρ), each split field is bounded there by M≥1, and K is nonempty compact in U.

Holomorphy means existence of a complex-linear total derivative; all complex-domain distances and field norms are Euclidean. Complex flow composition and inversion use compatible local germs or the same specified continuation branch.
For N≥2, b=ρ/(8N), r_N=ρ/(C₀MN), D_k=D(ρ/2−2bk), C₀=max(16,128d²), and the common retained domain is D(ρ/4).

X_j is the coefficient of h^(j−1) in L_N(h) applied to coordinates and divided by h. Thus even j vanish under symmetry, while the modified field and energy contain even powers of h. Primitives are normalized by H_j(0)=0.

Finite-time trajectory estimates allow signed h and use elapsed time n|h|; the analytic energy estimates use a fixed positive real h and assume retained numerical iterates. Additive residual bounds are deterministic hypotheses, not derived floating-point bounds.

load_bearing.statement: Analytic splitting data comprise bounded star-shaped U, a uniform holomorphic neighbourhood D(ρ), real analytic A,B with holomorphic extensions, split-field bounds M≥1, and nonempty compact K⊂U; Ψ_h is the partial composite φ_A^(h/2)∘φ_B^h∘φ_A^(h/2).

For a holomorphic F:D→Cⁿ bounded by M>0 and Δ_s(Z₀)⊂D, t₀=s/(8nM) gives a jointly holomorphic local solution family, displacement ≤M|t| on the closed t₀-disc, local uniqueness, and composition/inverse laws on compatible continuation branches.

The coefficient polynomials of the binomial pullback family preserve products and brackets; their derivatives at s=0 are local coefficient derivations satisfying D_jf=Σᵢ(D_jzᵢ)∂ᵢf, and agree with L_N through degree N.
On D(ρ/4), maxᵢ|(X_j)ᵢ|≤(8M/3)(C₀Mj/ρ)^(j−1); the coefficient fields are independent of truncation order. Euclidean field bounds include a factor √(2d).
For the stated analytic data and constants, 0<h≤a/3 and N=⌊a/h⌋ give, for sufficiently small h, an existing modified flow and ||Ψ_h(Z)−φ_Hh^h(Z)||≤CMh exp(−c/h) on D(ρ/8), with C independent of h,N.
For sufficiently small fixed positive h and z_j=Ψ_h^j(z₀)∈K through j=n, |H_h(z_n)−H_h(z₀)|≤Cnh exp(−c/h), and |H(z_n)−H(z₀)|≤Ch² if nh≤exp(c/(2h)).

For the stated C³ mechanical splitting on an open bounded convex tube W, compact K with positive tube margin, and finite bounds M₀,L₁,L₂, exact flow and Verlet agree through order two and ||V_h(z)−Φ_h(z)||≤C|h|³ uniformly on K for sufficiently small nonzero signed h.
For V:X→X with Lipschitz constant 1+Lh, h>0, matching initial points and per-step residual ≤η, d(x_n,z_n)≤η((1+Lh)^n−1)/(Lh) for L>0, or nη for L=0.

concerns.concern: Statement clause 3 says: “On the real part of D_N, H_h restricts to the corresponding real function with baseline H=A+B.” The inherited step domain permits complex h; real-valued primitives do not make their complex-weighted sum real. Explicitly, for d=1, A=p²/2 and B=q²/2 on a bounded ball, the drift-kick-drift matrix has logarithm coefficient X₃=(-p/12,-q/6), hence normalized H₃=q²/12−p²/24. With N=3 and sufficiently small h=ε(1+i)/√2, H_h(1,0)=1/2+iε²/12. Thus the reality assertion needs h real. The downstream optimal-truncation and energy results already impose positive real h.

Proof 1.1 says the slice is “continuous on its closure as the restriction of a continuous map,” referring to the open disc of radius ρ₁. The hypotheses give continuity only inside the open polydisc, not on its outer boundary; f(z)=1/(ρ₁−z) in one variable is a counterexample to that wording. The actual Cauchy application uses r₁<ρ₁ and needs continuity only on the smaller closed disc, so the argument survives without this assertion.

seams_checked.note: The phase-domain sign convention, finite C¹/C² canonical vocabulary and pointwise matrix/form equivalence agree with their suppliers. Numerical claims do not silently require smooth potentials.

Real local flows and signed composition laws are used with locally Lipschitz fields and actual existence domains. The finite-time recurrence explicitly invokes the supplier's qualified composition law.

The canonical-map definition and locality remark use exact-arithmetic canonical preservation and retain the numerical scope limitations. Page prose points to the full Cartesian-domain mechanical example, where whole drift/kick segments are admissible.

The Verlet example uses Q=R³, a C³ potential, explicit dimensionless normalization, finite tube bounds, sufficiently small signed steps and retention of both sequences. Its cubic local and quadratic finite-time bounds match the suppliers.

The numerical-error remark preserves the invariant state-set and separate numerical-map Lipschitz assumptions for residual accumulation, and the analytic small-step/compact-retention conditions for energy bounds. It distinguishes numerical predictions from measurements and model-to-system discrepancy.
